subject: MAP: Acme benchmarking playbook — regional latency & concurrency plan
messages:
From: Diego Fernandez <diego.fernandez@redwood.ai>
To: Sarah Green <sarah.green@acme-retail.com>
Cc: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.ai>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>, Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 10 Feb 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: MAP kickoff: Acme benchmarking playbook — regional latency & concurrency plan

Hi Sarah / Tom,

Thanks for agreeing to run the MAP evaluation with us. Attached is a single-sheet benchmarking playbook we propose to include in the mutual action plan. The goal: validate Redwood inference end-to-end for your peak retail workflows and confirm multi-region routing/failover behavior before contract signature.

High-level plan (see attachment for matrix):
- Objectives: measurable SLOs for P95 latency, TTFT (time-to-first-token), steady-state throughput, and concurrency limits. Verify failover latency when primary region unavailable.
- Regions: US (us-west), EU (eu-west), APAC (ap-southeast).
- Concurrency levels: 1, 8, 32, 128 (representative of storefront vs batch inference).
- Workloads: three payload types — short query (<=64 tokens), medium prompt (256 tokens), long context (1k tokens).
- Measurements: P50/P90/P95 latency, TTFT, tokens/sec, GPU utilization, error rate. Network RTT samples will be captured from Acme infra; please attach sample traces if available.

Acceptance criteria (proposed):
- P95 latency <= 350ms for short queries at concurrency 8 in primary region.
- TTFT <= 120ms for short queries.
- Failover to secondary region adds <= 200ms median additional latency.
- Error rate < 0.5% across tests.

Timeline (MAP milestones):
- Feb 10: Share playbook and test harness details (this email + attachment).
- Feb 12–16: Scheduling and network prep from Acme.
- Feb 17–20: Regional probes (low-priority windows) and targeted load runs.
- Feb 23: Consolidated results and recommended config.
- Feb 25: MAP sign-off and contract finalization gating.

Ask for Acme: please confirm target traffic windows for each region and attach 1–2 network trace samples (ping/traceroute/iperf). Also confirm if you want the Dedicated (reserved capacity) latency targets applied to this evaluation or the hosted defaults.

Thanks,
Diego
Account Executive, Redwood Inference

---
Attachment: 20260210-acme-map-performance-plan.xlsx (Excel; benchmarking matrix and measurement templates)

From: Sarah Green <sarah.green@acme-retail.com>
To: Diego Fernandez <diego.fernandez@redwood.ai>
Cc: Tom Meyers <tmeyers@acme-retail.com>
Date: Wed, 11 Feb 2026 10:47:00 -0800
Subject: Re: MAP kickoff: Acme benchmarking playbook — regional latency & concurrency plan

Diego — thanks, this looks good. A couple quick clarifications before we lock windows: 

1) For the failover scenario, can you confirm whether Redwood will perform DNS-based routing or active proxied routing with health-checked endpoints? We need to understand the expected failover delta.
2) Our infra team will provide RTT samples; attaching a short capture now. They prefer the runs to happen during Feb 18–19 (US peak off-hours) and Feb 20 for EU/APAC windows.

We prefer the hosted defaults for the evaluation since this will prove the out-of-the-box behavior — we'll evaluate Dedicated separately if the numbers warrant it.

Attaching: acme-net-trace-samples.zip

—Sarah
Director, Platform Engineering, Acme Retail

---
Attachment: acme-net-trace-samples.zip (zip; contains ping/traceroute samples)

From: Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.ai>
To: Diego Fernandez <diego.fernandez@redwood.ai>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>, Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 13 Feb 2026 08:22:00 -0800
Subject: Re: MAP kickoff: test harness and measurement details

Looping in some quick implementation notes for the test team so we can be ready for Feb 17–20 runs:

- Test harness: we'll use k6 for concurrency scaffolding + a lightweight collector that extracts TTFT from streamed SSE events. Scripts in the shared Drive link.
- For failover we plan two modes: (A) graceful region failover using routing policy that prefers primary region with active health checks, and (B) forced cutover emulating region blackout (route all traffic to fallback). Both will be timed and measured.
- We'll capture model-level metrics (token throughput, kv-cache hit ratio) and infra-level (GPU util, host-level latency) and annotate runs with RNG seeds/prompts so Acme can replay.
- Data export: CSV per-region with headers: run_id, region, concurrency, payload_type, p50_ms, p90_ms, p95_ms, ttft_ms, tokens_per_sec, error_rate

I'll prepare the k6 scenarios and drop them in the Drive by end of day Feb 16. Marcus — can you confirm the exact endpoint hostnames for EU/APAC so the scripts can pin regional IPs?

-priyom
Senior PM, Performance Engineering, Redwood Inference

From: Diego Fernandez <diego.fernandez@redwood.ai>
To: Sarah Green <sarah.green@acme-retail.com>
Cc: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.ai>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>, Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 17 Feb 2026 07:05:00 -0800
Subject: Re: MAP kickoff: scheduling regional probes (confirming windows)

Sarah — thanks for the trace. We scheduled the runs per your windows: US runs on Feb 18 (02:00–06:00 PT), EU on Feb 20 (01:00–05:00 CET), APAC on Feb 20 (02:00–06:00 SGT). 

Quick logistics:
- We will run the matrix at concurrency = [1, 8, 32, 128] across the three payload types. For each concurrency level we’ll do 3 repeats and record median P95 and TTFT.
- During the US window we’ll also perform forced cutover (simulated region failure) for a 15-minute period to validate failover delta and rollback.
- Engineers on call: Marcus (networking), Priyom (test harness), Karthik (routing policy). My role will be coordination and result sign-off.

Please confirm if the US window is still OK. If yes, we’ll kick off the low-load probes tonight and the full matrix tomorrow morning.

Thanks — looking forward to actionable numbers.
Diego
Account Executive, Redwood Inference

From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>
To: Sarah Green <sarah.green@acme-retail.com>, Diego Fernandez <diego.fernandez@redwood.ai>
Cc: Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>, Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 23 Feb 2026 11:44:00 -0800
Subject: Re: MAP — consolidated regional benchmarking results and recommended tuning

Hi Sarah / team — attaching the consolidated CSV with per-run metrics. Summary highlights below (all runs against hosted endpoints as requested):

US (us-west) — short query (<=64 tokens):
- Concurrency 8: P95 = 320ms, TTFT median = 110ms, tokens/sec = 480, error_rate = 0.2%
- Concurrency 128: P95 = 890ms, TTFT median = 240ms, tokens/sec = 1250, error_rate = 1.1% (above acceptance)

EU (eu-west) — short query:
- Concurrency 8: P95 = 370ms, TTFT = 130ms, tokens/sec = 430, error_rate = 0.3%

APAC (ap-southeast) — short query:
- Concurrency 8: P95 = 540ms, TTFT = 180ms, tokens/sec = 390, error_rate = 0.4%

Failover (forced cutover US->EU):
- Median additional latency observed during cutover = +180ms; peak delta = +420ms for a 30s window while caches warmed.

Recommended next steps / tuning: 
1) For Acme storefront SLAs, keep concurrency at 8 per inference worker or enable auto-burst to Dedicated in heavy campaigns (we can model cost impact).
2) Enable regional warm-up (pre-warm KV cache) for APAC during campaign start to reduce the 30s tail.
3) For global failover, we recommend health-check grace period of 10s and sticky-session allowance of 5s to reduce observed spikes.

We’re happy to walk through the CSV and proposed MAP language. If the numbers look acceptable, propose MAP sign-off on Feb 25 and commercial close by end of week.

Attachments: 20260223-acme-regional-results.csv

Regards,
Marcus Lin
Lead SRE, Redwood Inference
